paragraphs: Poole is covered by BCP Council, the council for Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, whose fostering service recruits and supports foster carers across the whole area. It is shown above with the independent agencies that work in Poole. BCP Council recruits only local residents as its own carers, so that children can stay close to home, keep their school and friendships, and stay in touch with their families.

In February 2026 the council backed What I Need Most, a campaign by Fostering South West, the regional partnership it belongs to. The council said then that around 280 children and young people were placed with its own carers, that it had more than 300 foster carers in over 200 households, and that 62% of those carers offer homes to children aged 11 and over. It warned that when no local foster home is free, children may have to be placed 20 miles or more from their community. The options it listed were full-time fostering, shared care, supported lodgings and short breaks.

The council says applicants from all backgrounds, ages and walks of life are welcome, whether single or in a couple, gay or straight, and that what matters most is offering a safe, stable and caring home. Its carers receive training, guidance, ongoing support and financial help. In December 2024 BCP launched its first Mockingbird group, in which several foster families are linked to an experienced hub carer who offers sleepovers where appropriate, peer support and shared activities.

Before you decide, talk to BCP Fostering and to two or three of the agencies above, and ask each about training, support and payments. Bournemouth, which is served by the same council, has its own page on this site.
